This article describe steps for crossreferencing using a real example from the state of Tasmania, Australia. Example data is provided as part of the package {ecoSynthesis}.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ecoSynthesis)
library(dplyr)
```


## Source and target classifications

We will use the Tasmanian vegetation communities described in the TASVEG 5.0 dataset. A look-up table for this dataset is available in the `TASVEG_LUT` data:

```{r}
#| label: load source classification
TASVEG_LUT
```

The target classification is the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology. A look-up table for this dataset is available in the `IUCN_GET_LUT` data:

```{r}
#| label: load target classification
#| eval: false
IUCN_GET_LUT
```

## Interpretation of classifications

In 2026 a group of four interpreters looked at full descriptions of the vegetation community units in the TASVEG 5.0 dataset and assigned them to ecosystem functional groups from the IUCN GET. A table containing source and target ids, membership values, and interpreter information (anonymised using codenames). This represents a first round of interpretation. The table is available in the `TASVEG_xref` data:

```{r}
#| label: load membership table
TASVEG_xref
```

### Our first membership table

If we want to use this data in our package we need to transform this table into a `membership_tbl` object. We explicitly declare which columns will be used as source and target ids, and which ones contain membership values and interpreter info.

```{r}
#| label: load membership table
TASVEG_memb <- membership_tbl(
  TASVEG_xref,
  source_id = "VEGCODE",
  target_id = "efg",
  membership = "memb",
  interpreter = "interp"
)
```

### Cleaning and preparing the data

This dataset has some errors that need to be curated:

- NA values in membership column
- some source units are invalid (valid id, but unit not aligned with ecosystem concept)
- some target ids are invalid (label does not exists in IUCN GET, likely typos)
